route_plan.route: Healthcare, diagnosis or treatment by a professional subject to secrecy
Direct processing by or under the responsibility of an A1 registered practitioner

final_review.reasoning:
The proposed processing is within Region A's scope: the identified name, date of birth, reference number, genetic report and ECG information are personal and sensitive information, and making the documents available to Harrow in Region B is an outward transfer. The A1 establishment also brings the processing within the Regulation even where access or storage occurs in Region B [f_6fcc5cd6b927] [f_72bdc3d5c28e] [f_7892b94ae5e8] [f_73d3eb94625a]. Articles 6 and 7 support the clinic's processing ground because the patient gave specific written consent for the named documents, recipient and second-opinion purpose, with withdrawal information [f_66d5f3ce3996] [f_4a28f229317f]. The sensitive-information requirement can be satisfied through the healthcare route: the second opinion concerns treatment, the A1 consultants are registered practitioners, and A1 law imposes professional secrecy [f_827ad358a031] [f_987ab471487e3] [A-REG 8#L1] [A-REG 8#L5] [A1-HIA 4#L1] [A1-HIA 5#L1]. The disclosure-specific secrecy condition is also satisfied by the patient's consent [A1-HIA 5#L2]. These processing and secrecy routes do not themselves authorise the outward transfer; Article 16 separately requires an applicable Article 17, 18 or 19 mechanism [A-REG 16#L1].

No such outward-transfer mechanism is available on the stated facts. Article 17 recognition is unavailable because Harrow has no Trusted Recipient Scheme certification and the recognition for Region B excludes sensitive information [f_febc895bce9e] [f_72bdc3d5c28e] [f_7892b94ae5e] [A-REG 17#L1] [A-REG 17#L3] [A-REG Annex II#L1]. Article 19(1)(a) cannot cover the genetic report because A1 law expressly prohibits making genetic information the subject of an outward transfer on that basis [A1-HIA 7#L1]. The patient's consent remains relevant to A1 professional secrecy and to ordinary processing, but it cannot substitute for the separate Article 16 outward-transfer requirement. The contract, vital-interest and public-interest derogations are not supported by the stated facts [A-REG 19#L1] [A-REG 19#L3] [A-REG 19#L4] [A-REG 19#L5].

Article 18 is also unavailable as described. No approved transfer-clause agreement exists [f_d75ec85c160f], and Article 18 requires executed approved clauses plus an assessment of third-territory law and supplementary measures where necessary [A-REG 18#L1] [A-REG 18#L2]. Harrow's portal activity is within the computing-provider definition [f_8c44c6e413c5] [B-RAA 2#L2] [B-RAA 2#L3]. Region B law permits a production order for records stored by or accessible to the computing provider, without court authorisation [B-RAA 3#L1] [B-RAA 3#L2], permits non-disclosure [B-RAA 4#L1], and removes statutory notice and review rights for the person concerned [B-RAA 6#L1]. The encryption provision only protects records where the provider does not hold and cannot obtain the keys; it does not provide equivalent protection against compelled production of records accessible to Harrow or against non-disclosure and lack of review [B-RAA 5#L1]. On the specialist assessment and the described portal arrangement, no effective supplementary measure providing essentially equivalent protection is identified. Article 18 therefore cannot be used [A-REG 18#L3].

The Region B Health Records Act does not add a current disclosure, service-agent, security or retention gate: the clinics are paid directly, Harrow keeps the referral in its own record for its own care, and it does not store records for another person [f_85110fb9a3e5] [f_3707d0e0f8a9] [f_7ddb7b6d46db]. Those facts fit the statutory limits for covered providers, service agents and data hosts [B-HRA 2#L3] [B-HRA 2#L4] [B-HRA 2#L5] [B-HRA 3#L1] [B-HRA 3#L2] [B-HRA 3#L3]. That non-application does not remove the separate Records Access Act issue relevant to assessing Article 18.

The remaining Region A duties do not cure the absent transfer mechanism. The general principles require lawful processing and demonstrable compliance [A-REG 5#L1] [A-REG 5#L7] [A-REG 5#L8], and the outward processing is unlawful as described because Article 16 is not satisfied. Article 11 information, Article 13 records and Article 14 security confirmations remain incomplete; the encrypted upload alone does not establish every risk-appropriate security measure [f_8c44c6e413c5] [A-REG 11#L1] [A-REG 11#L2] [A-REG 13#L1] [A-REG 14#L1]. The Article 12 high-risk determination also remains unresolved, although the A1 prescribed impact-assessment list is not engaged because this is not hosting or storage by an agent and does not involve insurer matching [f_a7a94423ed89] [A-REG 12#L1] [A-REG 12#L5] [A1-HIA 8#L1] [A1-HIA 8#L2] [A1-HIA 8#L3].
final_review.summary: The A1 healthcare-processing, consent, professional-secrecy and age requirements can be satisfied, and the Region B Health Records Act gates are not applicable. However, the transfer itself has no available Article 16-19 mechanism as described: recognition is unavailable, A1 bars the Article 19(1)(a) route for the genetic report, and Article 18 cannot be used without clauses and effective supplementary measures addressing Region B compulsory-access powers. The transfer must not proceed in its current form.
notes: The recognition, approved-clause and Article 19(1)(a) routes are outside the route plan because each is ruled out on the stated facts; they are not separate blockers. A different transfer architecture or a different legally available Article 16-19 route would require a fresh assessment.

The patient's consent supports ordinary processing and the A1 professional-secrecy disclosure condition, but it does not overcome the distinct A1-HIA 7 prohibition on using Article 19(1)(a) for an outward transfer of genetic information.

The Article 12 high-risk determination, complete Article 11 information, Article 13 processing records and full Article 14 security documentation remain required confirmations or duties identified by the specialists. They do not cure the absent outward-transfer mechanism.

The Region B production-order power is contingent, so it does not create a current Region B disclosure duty or a present production-order block. It is nevertheless material to the Article 18 law-and-practice assessment.

final_review.reasoning:
Region A law applies because the identified health and genetic information is processed by automated means in the context of Kestrel's A1 establishment, even though it will be made available in Region B (f_6fcc, f_12d62771fdeb, f_8c44c6e413c5). The treatment-related processing can be supported by the patient's specific consent and by the health-care route: the purpose is a treatment second opinion (f_110e981b0a7c, f_827ad358a031), and Kestrel's consultants are registered practitioners (f_987ab471487e). The consent also supports disclosure to Harrow under A1 professional-secrecy rules (f_66d5f3ce3996, f_2ecc11637ef3). These routes are compatible with Articles 6, 7 and 8 and A1-HIA sections 4 and 5. The genetic-outward-transfer prohibition does not prevent treatment processing, but it prevents reliance on Article 19(1)(a) for the outward transfer itself (A1-HIA 7#L1). The consent therefore cannot be the transfer route.

The transfer is an outward transfer because the information is sent to, stored in and accessed from a third territory (A-REG 4#L10; f_5aa17aaaa329, f_73d3eb94625a). Recognition is unavailable because Harrow lacks Trusted Recipient certification and the information is sensitive (f_febc895bce9e; f_72bdc3d5c28e, f_7892b94ae5e8; A-REG 17#L3; A-REG Annex II#L1). The compatible route is Article 18: the parties must execute approved clauses, assess third-territory law and practice, and adopt supplementary measures where necessary; if effective measures cannot be adopted, the transfer cannot proceed (A-REG 16#L1; A-REG 18#L1-A-REG 18#L3). Region B's findings do not engage the Health Records Act duties because neither clinic is a covered provider, service agent or data host on the supplied facts (B-HRA 2#L3-B-HRA 2#L5; B-HRA 3#L1-B-HRA 3#L3). They do not, however, resolve the unidentified portal operator's possible access or key arrangements.

The Article 18 route is capable of satisfying both Region A and A1 law, but it is not yet decidable as a complete route. No transfer-clause agreement exists (f_d75ec85c160f), and the Article 18 assessment cannot be completed for the portal arrangements because the portal operator, its access to the referral, and its access to encryption keys are not identified. The general Article 12(1) high-risk question is also unresolved. In addition, Region A's processing-principles, security, notice and records duties require the stated remedial actions before proceeding. These unresolved matters leave the combined outcome undetermined rather than demonstrating an incompatibility between the corpora.
final_review.summary: The transfer cannot presently be approved on the patient's consent alone. The patient's consent cannot be used as the Article 19(1)(a) outward-transfer derogation because the data includes genetic information and A1-HIA 7#L1 prohibits that route. The Article 19(1)(b) contract route remains unresolved because Kestrel's care terms say nothing about referrals outside Region A (f_91896785f7d3), and it is not selected.

The compatible route is Article 18. Under A-REG 16#L1 and A-REG 18#L1-L3, Kestrel and Harrow must execute the approved transfer clauses, complete the required assessment of Region B law and practice, and adopt supplementary measures if necessary. The answered Region B assessment identifies no current applicable obligation or event that would prevent Harrow from complying with those clauses on the described facts. This is therefore a resolvable route, not an incompatibility between the corpora. However, no approved clauses or other contract have been executed (f_d75ec85c160f), so the route is not yet operational.

A separate Article 12(1) question remains decisive. The transfer concerns identified genetic and health information and no impact assessment or separate high-risk determination has been prepared (f_7e86304fe561). The supplied facts establish that the express numerical and listed A1 categories are not triggered, but they do not establish whether this particular transfer is likely to result in a high risk. Under A-REG 12#L1 and A-REG 12#L4, that unresolved classification determines whether a pre-processing impact assessment is mandatory. The final conclusion is therefore undetermined rather than satisfiable_with_changes. If the high-risk issue is resolved and the assessment is completed where required, the Article 18 route can be combined with the other selected routes.
final_review.summary: Undetermined. Article 18 is a compatible outward-transfer route, but it requires executed approved clauses and supporting assessment measures. More importantly, no Article 12(1) high-risk determination has been supplied, so it cannot yet be decided whether a pre-processing impact assessment is mandatory. The Article 19(1)(a) consent route is unavailable for the genetic information.

blockers.gap: No Article 12(1) high-risk determination or impact assessment is supplied for the identified, sensitive one-off transfer. The facts establish that the transfer involves one person and is not one of the expressly listed large-scale or A1-listed categories, but they do not decide whether this transfer is likely to result in a high risk to the person's rights. That determination is necessary to decide whether the pre-processing assessment duty applies under A-REG 12#L1.
blockers.why_not_a_confirmation: This is not merely an omitted element of an otherwise supplied assessment. The unresolved likelihood-of-high-risk determination changes whether a mandatory pre-processing assessment exists at all; confirming only the transfer's one-off nature or the use of encryption would not decide that conditional requirement.

notes: Before relying on Article 18, execute the Commission-approved clauses and complete and document the assessment of Region B law and practice required by A-REG 18#L2; adopt effective supplementary measures if necessary. Do not proceed under Article 18 if effective supplementary measures cannot be adopted under A-REG 18#L3.

The Article 19(1)(a) consent derogation is a ruled-out fallback, not part of the route plan. The patient's consent remains usable for ordinary processing, sensitive-information processing and A1 third-party disclosure, but it cannot authorize this genetic-information outward transfer under A1-HIA 7#L1.

Before proceeding, update the patient information to identify the selected Article 18 route, the approved clauses and any supplementary measures, together with the Article 11 information; prepare the written processing records identifying the outward-transfer route; and confirm that the technical and organisational security measures are appropriate. These are implementation conditions and do not create a separate cross-jurisdiction conflict.

The Article 19(1)(b) contract route is an unselected fallback. It could be considered only if evidence establishes that the external transfer is necessary for performance of the patient's contract with Kestrel and remains occasional under A-REG 19#L3 and A-REG 19#L6.

The A1 hosting/storage conditions are not engaged because Harrow keeps the referral in its own clinical record for its own care rather than hosting or storing Kestrel's records for Kestrel (f_a7a94423ed89, f_3707d0e0f8a).
